messages:
alex: heads-up — after landing attn-kernel-v3 I'm seeing intermittent OOMs in the long-chat E2E tests. repro is stable on my machine with a 6k prefix + kv-cache warmup. attaching quick notes below.

alex: repro steps: run local perf harness with model=redwood/open-attn-v3, seq=6144, batch=1, kv_warmup=true. failure within ~120s.

tara: thanks. can you paste TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF and the exact launcher args?

alex: sure:
```
TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=garbage_collection_threshold:0.8,max_split_size_mb:128,allow_growth:0
python -m perf.harness --model open-attn-v3 --seq 6144 --batch 1 --kv-warmup --trace=ptprof
```

ravi: hm, expandable_segments is the one we changed last week in runtime defaults, right? what's that env set to?

alex: I didn't set expandable_segments explicitly (using default). From runtime logs it looks like expandable_segments=0 (no segment expansion).

lee: that combination is interesting — no expandable segments + big max_split_size_mb can force allocator to hand out large contiguous blocks and then fragmentation explodes when KV buffers are freed/reused. KV warmup causes repeated large allocations, which are not reclaimed efficiently.

alex: here's the memory summary from the failing run (trimmed):
```
|   GPU 0 Memory Summary
|   allocated: 9.34 GiB
|   reserved: 11.12 GiB
|   active allocations: 462
|   fragmentation: 1.78 GiB
|   peak allocated: 10.1 GiB
```

alex: profiler snippet (ptprof):
```
Alloc % | Function
42%     | kv_cache_allocate
19%     | attention_forward_kernel_v3
12%     | workspace_reserve
```

tara: that points at KV cache + workspace interplay. two hypotheses: (A) lack of expandable_segments prevents in-place split, causing max_split_size_mb to be ineffective; (B) GC threshold too high delays freeing, so reserved memory keeps growing across requests.

ravi: agree. quick experiment matrix: try {expandable_segments=1, max_split_size_mb=32, gc_thresh=0.6} vs {expandable_segments=0, max_split_size_mb=64, gc_thresh=0.8}. measure tail latency and OOM rate.

alex: ran first combo overnight: expandable_segments=1,max_split_size_mb=32,garbage_collection_threshold=0.6. result: no OOMs, fragmentation down to ~600MB, but p50 latency +3% and p99 +7%.

lee: latency hit probably from extra kernel invocations (smaller splits -> more kernel launches) and extra bookkeeping in allocator. we need to trade off tail SLO vs reliability.

tara: can we compensate in batching heuristics? e.g., cap continuous token growth per slot or prefer coalesced requests for long prefix workloads so we avoid many simultaneous large allocations. maybe a special codepath when kv_warmup=true to preallocate a stable slab for KV and mark it non-evictable.

ravi: also try a hybrid: enable expandable_segments but raise max_split_size_mb to 48. That keeps larger chunks but allows splits when required. Also lower gc_thresh to 0.65 so we don't hoard too long.

alex: ran hybrid: expandable_segments=1,max_split_size_mb=48,gc_thresh=0.65 -> no OOMs, frag ~800MB, p50 baseline, p99 +2%. promising.

perf-bot: perf test 492: canary run with hybrid config -> 1/50 tasks saw 5% p99 spike, 0 OOMs.

lee: plan: canary rollout for 10% traffic with hybrid config + add a runtime metric for "large-allocation-count" (>max_split_size_mb). If that metric spikes, auto-fallback to previous config.

tara: also add a lightweight probe in the runtime to log when KV cache allocations exceed 75% of a segment size; this will help us validate the prealloc idea.

ravi: follow-ups: (1) add experiment matrix and results to the perf board (owner: ravi) (2) implement metric and auto-fallback (owner: lee) (3) prototype KV prealloc slab for warmup (owner: alex) (4) do 24h canary and report.

alex: I'll push the small config patch and smoke test on staging now. dropping the exact commands here for reproducibility: 
```
# hybrid config
export TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=garbage_collection_threshold:0.65,max_split_size_mb:48
runtime_flags="--expandable_segments=1 --kv-warmup-slab=0"
# run harness
python -m perf.harness --model open-attn-v3 --seq 6144 --batch 1 --kv-warmup --runtime-args "$runtime_flags" --out=hybrid-run.json
```

lee: nice. keep notes short in the perf board, add raw memory summaries and pprof stacks. prefer human-readable artefacts + numeric results.

alex: will do. thanks all.

tara: thanks — if canary looks good let's bake hybrid defaults into the private deployment templates and add a docs note about the allocator knobs and KV warmup interaction.

ravi: filed follow-ups in task tracker: INF-2187 (experiment matrix), INF-2188 (metric + fallback), INF-2189 (KV prealloc POC).

alex: closing loop once 24h canary finishes, will post final stats. :thumbsup:
